english.notes:
(i) Section 8(2) of the Human Tissue Act 2004 exempts from the offence a person who reasonably believes that what he uses or stores is not donated material.
(ii) Section 8(4) of the Act provides that references to a qualifying purpose are to
(a) a purpose specified in Schedule 1,
(b) the purpose of medical diagnosis or treatment,
(c) the purpose of decent disposal, or
(d) a purpose specified in regulations made by the Secretary of State.
(iii) Section 8(5) of the Act provides that references to donated material are to the body of the deceased person or relevant material which has come from a human body which is, or has been, the subject of donation.
(iv) Section 8(6) of the Act provides that a body, or material, is the subject of donation if authority under section 1(1) to (3) of the Act exists in relation to it.

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Three years imprisonment and/or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
